content.title: About
content.content: Ramen bowl is a ready‑to‑cook ramen kit in a bowl, containing dried noodles, a broth packet, aromatic seasonings and often dried vegetables. It is designed for quick preparation of hot ramen in 3–5 minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The NFS (National Food Service) brand distributes ramen bowls in over 20 countries.
Each serving provides about 350 kcal, making it a convenient snack for students and office workers.
The kit often includes a “black garlic” spice, popular in Asian cuisine.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, and some variants use biodegradable materials.
In Japan ramen bowls are frequently served with a boiled egg, but the NFS version omits the egg for longer shelf life.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: The dried noodles supply carbohydrates that are rapidly converted into energy, useful for an active lifestyle.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: A typical kit contains 8–10 g of protein, helping to maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Minerals and vitamins
items.content: The broth packet is fortified with iron, potassium and B‑vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Most NFS ramen varieties contain less than 5 g of fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Convenient storage
items.content: The dry product can be stored up to 12 months at room temperature without refrigeration.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The broth packet may contain up to 900 mg of sodium, exceeding daily recommendations for people with hypertension.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
items.content: MSG is commonly added and can cause headaches or a tingling sensation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The kit may contain soy sauce, wheat and seafood; those with corresponding allergies should check the label.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of dry noodles can cause bloating in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bring 400 ml of water to a boil, add the dried noodles and cook for 3–4 minutes. Drain some water if you prefer a thicker broth, then stir in the broth packet, seasonings and dried vegetables. Mix well and let stand for 1–2 minutes. Optionally top with a boiled egg, sliced green onion or chili.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly to prevent moisture ingress.
